digoxin.t: During simvastatin initiation, monitor digoxin levels.
Concomitant use of digoxin with simvastatin may result in elevated plasma digoxin concentrations [ see CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY ( 12.3 ) ].

amiodarone.t: The risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis is increased by concomitant use of amiodarone, dronedarone, ranolazine, or calcium channel blockers with simvastatin.
Amiodarone, Dronedarone, Ranolazine, or Calcium Channel Blockers Clinical Impact:

amlodipine.t: For patients taking amiodarone, amlodipine, or ranolazine, do not exceed simvastatin 20 mg daily [see DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION ( 2.5 )] .
Simvastatin dosage modifications are recommended for patients taking lomitapide, verapamil, diltiazem, dronedarone, amiodarone, amlodipine or ranolazine [see DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION ( 2.5 )].

ezetimibe.t: In a clinical study (median follow-up 3.9 years) of patients at high risk of CVD and with well-controlled LDL-C levels on simvastatin 40 mg/day with or without ezetimibe 10 mg/day, there was no incremental benefit on cardiovascular outcomes with the addition of lipid-modifying doses of niacin.

colchicine.t: Cases of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis have been reported with concomitant use of colchicine with simvastatin.
Consider if the benefit of using colchicine concomitantly with simvastatin outweighs the increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.

warfarin.t: There are postmarketing reports of clinically evident bleeding and/or increased INR in patients taking concomitant statins and warfarin.

glucose.t: 5.4 Increases in HbA1c and Fasting Serum Glucose Levels Increases in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels have been reported with statins, including simvastatin.

statin.t: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS Simvastatin is contraindicated in the following conditions:
Hypersensitivity to simvastatin or any excipients in simvastatin tablets USP.

anticoag.t: Simvastatin may potentiate the effect of coumarin anticoagulants and increase the INR.
The concomitant use of simvastatin (20 to 40 mg) and coumarin anticoagulants increased the INR from a baseline of 1.7 to 1.8 in healthy subjects and from 2.6 to 3.4 in patients with hyperlipidemia.
